name: Parallel panels for non-comparable bases
reader_question: How do the same subjects compare on bases that cannot share an axis or a total?
relationship: Side-by-side comparison across independent bases; each panel has its own zero-based axis and unit.
use_when: Funding, capacity and counts describe the same subjects but cannot be added or indexed together
The reader should see that rankings differ by basis
avoid_when: Two panels carry the same basis — they are one chart
A combined score or total is wanted; this pattern refuses to imply one

data_contract.notes: Distinct basis name and its unit; identical bases are rejected
Each panel orders its own bars by value
One subject highlighted consistently across panels

units: Each panel has its own unit and zero-based axis; no value is compared across panels.

editable: One bar chart per panel with embedded workbook (Edit Data)
not_data_bound: Panel headings, unit lines and separator rules are text and shapes drawn from the fixture

table_alternative: A matrix of subjects by basis with the unit in each column heading.
variations: Two panels for a before-and-after basis change
Dot plots per panel for many subjects
limitations: Bar lengths are not comparable between panels and a shared bar scale would mislead
Differing ranks do not explain why the bases differ

excluded_alternatives.reason: A second axis implies a relationship and invites false crossings
Weights bases that cannot be added; SMPT has no synthetic scores
